(a) the most significant predictors of quality of life are family interactions, depression, and medication side effects; and (b) quality of life is significantly associated with medication compliance.
better quality of life was associated with fewer depressive symptomatology and fewer medication side effects and that better family relationships also predicted better quality of life.

the quality of life for seriously mentally ill persons can be improved through interventions that focus on reducing depressive symptoms, reducing medication side effects, increasing social skills, improving family interactions, and increasing social support.

quality of life in the seriously mentally ill population is related to clinical factors such as medication compliance, social skills, and family interactions, and to demographic factors such as age, gender, and marital status.

the clinical variables that are most strongly associated with quality of life in persons with serious mental illness are depressive symptoms, medication side effects, family interactions, and medication compliance.
the results of this research indicate that the clinical characteristics of the seriously mentally ill are related to the quality of life they report.

the quality of life is associated with the clinical characteristics of the patients.
quality of life is a multidimensional concept and that the most important clinical factors that affect quality of life are depressive symptoms and side-effects of medication.

quality of life is a multifaceted construct that includes both objective and subjective components and that the objective and subjective components are not always highly correlated.
